title: Decoder
body:
An $n$-to-$2^n$ [[Combinational Logic|combinational]] circuit: read the $n$ input lines as
a binary number, assert exactly one of the $2^n$ output lines, leave the rest low. A
2-to-4 decoder:

| $A_1$ | $A_0$ | $Y_3 Y_2 Y_1 Y_0$ |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| 0 | 0 | 0001 |
| 0 | 1 | 0010 |
| 1 | 0 | 0100 |
| 1 | 1 | 1000 |

Exactly the inverse of an [[Encoder]], which takes one-hot in and gives binary out.

The everyday use is address decoding: the high bits of an address go into a decoder whose
outputs are the chip-select lines, which is how a [[CPU]] putting one address on the
[[System Bus]] activates exactly one [[ROM]] chip, RAM chip, or [[I-O Interface]]. That is
the mechanism [[Memory Mapping]] is built on.
